record.original_question: What geometric assumptions imply that a metric (possibly, of a fixed signature) on a closed manifold is geodesically complete?

evidence.quote: What geometric assumptions imply that a metric (possibly, of a fixed signature) on a closed manifold is geodesically complete?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth closed (compact, without boundary) manifold equipped with a smooth pseudo-Riemannian metric $g$ of fixed signature $(p,q)$. Recall that $g$ is said to be geodesically complete if every maximal geodesic $\gamma:I\to M$ of the Levi-Civita connection of $g$ is defined on all of $\mathbb{R}$. While every Riemannian metric on a closed manifold is geodesically complete by the Hopf–Rinow theorem, this conclusion fails in indefinite signature: there exist closed manifolds carrying smooth Lorentzian (and more general pseudo-Riemannian) metrics that are geodesically incomplete.

Problem. Identify natural geometric conditions on a pseudo-Riemannian metric $g$ of fixed signature $(p,q)$ on a closed manifold $M$ that imply $g$ is geodesically complete. More precisely, find general structural hypotheses—such as conditions on the curvature, holonomy, isometry group, parallel tensor fields, or symmetry assumptions—under which every metric of signature $(p,q)$ on a closed manifold satisfying these hypotheses is necessarily geodesically complete, going beyond known cases (e.g., compact homogeneous Lorentzian manifolds, or compact Lorentzian manifolds of constant sectional curvature).
artifact.status_search_result: The question of which geometric assumptions force geodesic completeness of an indefinite metric on a closed manifold is widely regarded as open in Lorentzian and semi-Riemannian geometry. Hopf–Rinow has no pseudo-Riemannian analogue, and the various notions of Lorentzian completeness are independent (Kundt, Geroch, Beem). Only partial positive results are known (e.g., compact homogeneous Lorentzian manifolds are complete; compact Lorentzian manifolds of constant curvature are complete), and recent surveys and problem lists (Burns–Matveev; overviews on Lorentzian completeness) continue to list this as an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems and Questions about Geodesics (Burns–Matveev)
status_evidence.snippet: Problem list including questions on geometric assumptions implying geodesic completeness on closed manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in a curated geodesics problem list.

status_evidence.title: An overview of (completeness in) Lorentzian geometry (I. Terek)
status_evidence.snippet: There is no Hopf–Rinow analogue; the three types of Lorentzian completeness are logically independent (Kundt 1963, Geroch 1968, Beem 1976).
status_evidence.claim: Foundational obstacles make general completeness criteria nontrivial; only partial results are known.

status_evidence.title: Completeness conditions for spacetimes with low-regularity metrics
status_evidence.snippet: For Lorentzian manifolds the completeness conditions are considerably more involved and many fundamental questions remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature confirms that completeness criteria for indefinite metrics remain an active open area.

status_evidence.title: The geodesic completeness of compact Lorentzian manifolds (de la Fuente)
status_evidence.snippet: Partial results: e.g., compact homogeneous Lorentzian manifolds and compact Lorentzian manifolds of constant curvature are geodesically complete.
status_evidence.claim: Only specific classes are known to be complete, leaving the general question open.
